scenario.title: Vendor Meeting and Improvement Action Follow-up
scenario.initial_description: The team meets with an equipment vendor to discuss improvement ideas. After the meeting, someone summarizes the discussion and follows up on action items.

reference_workflow.goal: Coordinate a vendor meeting, capture improvement decisions, and track follow-up actions.

activities.name: Assign action-item owners and due dates

decisions.condition: Is the proposed improvement technically feasible?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Meeting scheduling can be assisted by calendar availability checks.
Meeting notes can be summarized into decisions, open questions, and action items.
Action-item reminders and status tracking can be automated.

activities.name: Prepare Meeting Agenda and Supporting Materials
Conduct Vendor Meeting
activities.actor: Team Lead, Team Members, Vendor Representative
activities.system: Video Conferencing Tool or Physical Meeting

activities.name: Review and Validate Meeting Summary
outputs: Validated action item list with owners and due dates

activities.name: Distribute Meeting Summary and Action Items
outputs: Action item notifications sent to owners

activities.name: Log Action Items in Tracking System
outputs: Logged action items with assigned owners, due dates, and status

activities.name: Send Follow-up Reminders to Action Item Owners
Collect and Review Action Item Completion Evidence
inputs: Supporting evidence or deliverables from owners

activities.name: Escalate Unresolved or High-Risk Action Items
Close Out Meeting and Archive Documentation

decisions.condition: Is the meeting summary accurate and complete?
branches: Yes - Proceed to distribute summary and action items (A6)
No - Return to note taker for revision (A4)

decisions.condition: Are action items overdue or approaching their due date?
Are all action items completed and verified?
branches: Yes - Proceed to close out and archive (A12)
No - Assess if escalation is needed (D4)

decisions.condition: Do unresolved action items pose significant risk or require management involvement?
branches: No - Continue monitoring and reminders (A8, A9)

exceptions: Vendor cancels or reschedules the meeting at short notice, requiring rescheduling of all participants
Key stakeholder is absent during the meeting, leading to incomplete decision-making
Meeting notes are lost or not captured adequately, requiring reconstruction from memory
Action item owner is unavailable or has left the organization, requiring reassignment
Vendor fails to follow through on commitments made during the meeting
Improvement ideas raised require budget approval beyond team authority, causing delays
Meeting summary contains disputed information, requiring mediation between parties

automation_opportunities.rationale: Meeting scheduling can be automated using calendar integration tools that check availability across participants and propose optimal slots, reducing back-and-forth coordination effort.
constraints: Vendor must use a compatible scheduling system or accept calendar invitations
Time zone differences may complicate automated slot selection

automation_opportunities.target: A4 - Capture and Summarize Meeting Discussion
automation_opportunities.rationale: AI-powered transcription and summarization tools can automatically generate structured meeting summaries and draft action item lists from recorded or transcribed meeting audio, significantly reducing manual note-taking effort.
constraints: Meeting must be conducted via a platform supporting transcription
Vendor participants must consent to recording
AI-generated summaries require human review for accuracy

automation_opportunities.target: A6 - Distribute Meeting Summary and Action Items
automation_opportunities.rationale: Once the summary is approved, automated distribution via email or collaboration platform can be triggered without manual intervention, using predefined distribution lists.
constraints: Distribution list must be maintained and up to date
Approval from Team Lead must be confirmed before triggering automation

automation_opportunities.target: A7 - Log Action Items in Tracking System
automation_opportunities.rationale: Action items identified during meeting summarization can be automatically parsed and logged into a task tracking system with assigned owners and due dates, eliminating duplicate manual data entry.
required_data: Validated action item list with owners and due dates
Task tracking system API or integration
constraints: Action item owners must exist as users in the tracking system
Integration between document management and task tracking systems required

automation_opportunities.target: D2 and A9 - Monitor Action Item Progress and Send Follow-up Reminders
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated deadline monitoring and reminder notifications can be scheduled based on due dates logged in the tracking system, removing the need for manual coordinator intervention for routine follow-ups.
required_data: Logged action items with due dates and owner contact information
Status update data from tracking system
constraints: Tracking system must support automated notification rules
Escalation thresholds and reminder frequency must be configured upfront

automation_opportunities.rationale: A dashboard aggregating action item statuses from the tracking system can provide real-time visibility to the Team Lead without requiring manual status collection, reducing oversight effort.
constraints: All updates must be entered into the tracking system by owners for data to be reliable
Dashboard tool must integrate with the task tracking system

automation_opportunities.target: A11 - Escalate Unresolved or High-Risk Action Items
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated escalation alerts can be generated when action items exceed defined risk thresholds or remain overdue beyond a configurable period, ensuring management is notified without relying on manual judgment alone.
constraints: Risk categorization rules must be defined and maintained
Escalation policy must be agreed upon and approved by management

automation_opportunities.target: A12 - Close Out Meeting and Archive Documentation
automation_opportunities.rationale: When all action items are verified as complete, an automated workflow can trigger archiving of the meeting record and action item log to the document management system, reducing manual close-out steps.
required_data: Archive folder structure in document management system
constraints: Archiving logic must correctly identify all items as closed before triggering
Document management system must support automated file organization

assumptions: The team and vendor conduct meetings on a recurring or project-driven basis, making process standardization worthwhile.
A document management system exists for storing meeting materials and summaries.
A task or action item tracking system is available or can be adopted by the team.
The Team Lead has authority to approve meeting summaries and escalate action items without requiring additional approvals from higher management in routine cases.
Vendor participants are external and may not have access to internal systems, limiting integration with vendor-side tools.
Meeting frequency is assumed to be periodic (e.g., monthly or quarterly) rather than ad hoc, though the process applies to either.
Action item owners are identifiable individuals within the team or vendor organization who can be contacted directly.
The organization uses a collaboration platform (e.g., email or team messaging tool) for notifications and distribution.
Recording vendor meetings for transcription purposes requires consent and is subject to organizational and legal policies.
Improvement ideas discussed in meetings may require separate approval workflows if they involve significant investment or operational changes, which are out of scope for this workflow.

missing_information.gap: No specific roles are identified for meeting participants (e.g., who from the team attends, which vendor representatives are involved, who is responsible for the summary)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without defined actors, it is impossible to assign ownership of tasks, determine authorization levels, or map the workflow to specific job functions for automation targeting

missing_information.gap: No systems or tools are mentioned for scheduling the meeting, capturing notes, distributing summaries, or tracking action items
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation potential depends heavily on whether existing platforms (e.g., calendaring, note-taking, task management) are already in use or need to be introduced

missing_information.gap: The format, destination, and required content of the meeting summary are undefined
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automating summary generation or distribution requires knowing the expected output structure, recipients, and storage location

missing_information.gap: There is no information about what materials or data are prepared or shared before or during the meeting (e.g., agendas, improvement proposals, equipment data)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Pre-meeting inputs affect what can be automated in preparation steps and what data sources need to be integrated

missing_information.gap: No decision criteria are defined for evaluating or prioritizing improvement ideas raised during the meeting
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without decision logic, it is unclear how action items are selected, escalated, or rejected, making it difficult to model branching paths or automate approvals

missing_information.gap: Meeting cadence and follow-up timelines are not specified
missing_information.why_it_matters: Frequency determines the volume of process instances and affects the ROI calculation for automation investment

missing_information.gap: The effort involved in summarizing the discussion and following up on action items is not quantified
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without effort estimates, it is not possible to assess how much time could be saved through automation or prioritize this process against others

missing_information.gap: No exception handling is described for scenarios such as missed follow-ups, unresolved action items, vendor non-response, or meeting cancellations
missing_information.why_it_matters: Exception paths are critical for building robust automated workflows and ensuring process continuity

missing_information.gap: Dependencies between this workflow and upstream or downstream processes (e.g., maintenance planning, procurement, approval chains) are not mentioned
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation of follow-up actions may trigger or require input from adjacent processes, which must be mapped to avoid integration gaps

missing_information.gap: No approval mechanism is defined for acting on improvement ideas or committing resources based on vendor recommendations
missing_information.why_it_matters: Approvals introduce human-in-the-loop requirements that constrain what can be fully automated and must be reflected in the process model

missing_information.gap: It is unclear whether meeting notes and action items are recorded in a structured or unstructured format, and whether historical records exist
missing_information.why_it_matters: Structured data enables automation and analytics; unstructured notes would require NLP capabilities and add complexity to any automation solution

clarification_questions.question: Who are the defined roles responsible for organizing the meeting, capturing notes during the session, and producing the formal summary afterward?
What tools or systems are currently used to schedule meetings, record discussion notes, distribute summaries, and track action items to completion?
What is the expected format and required content of the meeting summary, and who are its intended recipients?
How are improvement ideas evaluated and prioritized after the meeting, and who has the authority to approve resource commitments or next steps?
How often do these vendor meetings occur, and what is the expected turnaround time for delivering the summary and completing follow-up actions?
What happens when action items are not completed on time or when the vendor does not respond to follow-up requests — is there an escalation path?
